You are implementing the AES block cipher core for a Python-to-Node port.

Read /workspace/harness/SPEC.md FIRST — it is the measured behavioral contract for this port. Everything in it was empirically verified against /workspace/dataset/test15_executable; treat it as ground truth and never contradict it.

HARD RULES (violating any one invalidates the whole deliverable):
- ESM only. Use import/export. NEVER use require(), module.exports, __dirname, or CommonJS anything.
- Every file you create MUST use the .mjs extension, and every relative import MUST include the .mjs suffix.
- ZERO external/npm dependencies. Only node: builtins (node:fs, node:path, node:process, node:url) and local relative imports.
- node:crypto is ABSOLUTELY FORBIDDEN — do not import it, do not reference Cipher/Decipher/createCipheriv/webcrypto anywhere, not even in a comment. AES must be implemented by hand from FIPS-197.
- Do NOT shell out to python, and do NOT embed or execute python.
- All deliverable code goes under /output. Never write deliverables anywhere else.
- Target Node 18.19: no Array.prototype.toSorted/findLast on typed arrays, no RegExp /v flag, no Object.groupBy.
- Write clean, documented, production-quality library code. Each module gets a short header comment explaining what Python behavior it reproduces.
- Use the Write tool to create files. Do not print code to stdout as your answer.

Create EXACTLY these four files, with EXACTLY these exported interfaces (other agents import them, so the signatures are contractual and must not drift):

--- /output/lib/aes/galois.mjs ---
  export function xtime(a)      // a is 0..255; multiply by x in GF(2^8) with the AES reduction polynomial 0x11b
  export function gmul(a, b)    // GF(2^8) product of two bytes
  export function ginv(a)       // multiplicative inverse in GF(2^8); ginv(0) === 0 by AES convention

--- /output/lib/aes/tables.mjs ---
  export const SBOX      // Uint8Array(256)
  export const INV_SBOX  // Uint8Array(256)
  export const RCON      // Uint8Array(11) where RCON[i] for i>=1 is x^(i-1) in GF(2^8): 01 02 04 08 10 20 40 80 1b 36
  export const MUL2, MUL3, MUL9, MUL11, MUL13, MUL14   // Uint8Array(256) lookup tables for MixColumns / InvMixColumns

  CRITICAL: derive SBOX algorithmically at module load (multiplicative inverse in GF(2^8) followed by the
  affine transform b ^ rotl(b,1) ^ rotl(b,2) ^ rotl(b,3) ^ rotl(b,4) ^ 0x63) using galois.mjs. Do NOT paste a
  hardcoded table. Then assert the derivation with a handful of known FIPS-197 values
  (SBOX[0x00]=0x63, SBOX[0x01]=0x7c, SBOX[0x10]=0xca, SBOX[0x53]=0xed, SBOX[0x7f]=0xd2, SBOX[0xff]=0x16)
  and assert INV_SBOX[SBOX[i]] === i for all i. Throw an Error if any assertion fails.

--- /output/lib/aes/errors.mjs ---
  export class InvalidKeySizeError extends Error   // message defaults to 'Invalid key size'
  export class InvalidBlockSizeError extends Error // constructor(message) — caller supplies the exact text
  Keep this layer free of any Python/traceback concepts; the pyaes shim maps these to Python exceptions.

--- /output/lib/aes/key-schedule.mjs ---
  export const BLOCK_SIZE = 16
  export const ROUNDS_BY_KEY_SIZE  // Map: 16->10, 24->12, 32->14
  export function isValidKeySize(byteLength)
  export function expandKey(keyBytes)
    // keyBytes: Uint8Array. Throws InvalidKeySizeError when the length is not 16/24/32.
    // Returns { keySize, rounds, roundKeys } where roundKeys is an Array of (rounds+1) Uint8Array(16),
    // each already in the SAME byte order as the 16-byte input block, so AddRoundKey is a plain
    // 16-way XOR with no transposition. Implement the standard FIPS-197 word-oriented schedule
    // (RotWord/SubWord/Rcon, plus the extra SubWord every 8 words for 256-bit keys).

--- /output/lib/aes/block-cipher.mjs ---
  export { BLOCK_SIZE }
  export class AES {
    constructor(keyBytes)          // Uint8Array; throws InvalidKeySizeError for bad lengths
    get keySize()                  // 16 | 24 | 32
    get rounds()                   // 10 | 12 | 14
    encryptBlock(block)            // Uint8Array(16) in -> new Uint8Array(16) out; must NOT mutate the input
    decryptBlock(block)            // Uint8Array(16) in -> new Uint8Array(16) out; must NOT mutate the input
  }
  Standard FIPS-197 cipher and equivalent-inverse-free straightforward inverse cipher:
  encrypt = AddRoundKey, then (rounds-1) x [SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, AddRoundKey], then
  [SubBytes, ShiftRows, AddRoundKey].
  decrypt = AddRoundKey(last), then (rounds-1) x [InvShiftRows, InvSubBytes, AddRoundKey, InvMixColumns],
  then [InvShiftRows, InvSubBytes, AddRoundKey(first)].
  Throw a TypeError if block.length !== 16 (the pyaes layer checks sizes before calling, so this is
  only a defensive internal guard).

--- /output/lib/aes/index.mjs ---
  Re-export AES, BLOCK_SIZE, expandKey, isValidKeySize, ROUNDS_BY_KEY_SIZE and the two error classes.

Then SELF-TEST before you finish. Write a scratch script to /tmp (NOT /output) that imports your modules and
checks the FIPS-197 Appendix B/C known-answer vectors:
  AES-128 key 000102...0f, plaintext 00112233445566778899aabbccddeeff -> 69c4e0d86a7b0430d8cdb78070b4c55a
  AES-192 key 000102...17, same plaintext -> dda97ca4864cdfe06eaf70a0ec0d7191
  AES-256 key 000102...1f, same plaintext -> 8ea2b7ca516745bfeafc49904b496089
  FIPS-197 Appendix B: AES-128 key 2b7e151628aed2a6abf7158809cf4f3c, plaintext 3243f6a8885a308d313198a2e0370734 -> 3925841d02dc09fbdc118597196a0b32
Also check decryptBlock(encryptBlock(x)) === x for many random blocks and all three key sizes.
Run it with node and iterate until every vector passes. Report the final pass/fail lines.

Your final message: one short paragraph listing the files you created and the KAT results.

1	# Behavioral spec — `/workspace/dataset/test15.py` → `/output/test15.mjs`
2	
3	All facts below were **empirically measured** from `/workspace/dataset/test15_executable`.
4	Do not re-derive them; do not contradict them.
5	
6	## 0. The program
7	
8	```python
9	parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
10	parser.add_argument('--key1', type=str, required=True)
11	parser.add_argument('--key2', type=str, required=True)
12	parser.add_argument('--data', type=str, required=True)
13	args = parser.parse_args()
14	aes1 = pyaes.AESModeOfOperationECB(args.key1.encode())   # source line 12
15	aes2 = pyaes.AESModeOfOperationECB(args.key2.encode())   # source line 13
16	ciphertext = aes1.encrypt(args.data.encode())            # source line 14
17	wrong_plaintext = aes2.decrypt(ciphertext)               # source line 15
18	print(ciphertext)                                        # source line 16
19	print(wrong_plaintext)                                   # source line 17
20	```
21	
22	Success output (stdout, exit 0) is exactly two lines, each `repr(bytes)` + `\n`.
23	
24	## 1. Order of operations (matters for which error wins)
25	
26	1. parse args (argparse errors → exit **2**)
27	2. `args.key1.encode()` → may raise `UnicodeEncodeError` (exit 1, traceback line 12)
28	3. `AESModeOfOperationECB(key1)` → may raise `ValueError: Invalid key size` (exit 1, line 12)
29	4. `args.key2.encode()` / `AESModeOfOperationECB(key2)` → same, line 13
30	5. `args.data.encode()` → `UnicodeEncodeError` (line 14)
31	6. `aes1.encrypt(data)` → `ValueError: plaintext block must be 16 bytes` (line 14)
32	7. `aes2.decrypt(ciphertext)` — ciphertext is always 16 bytes, so unreachable
33	8. two `print`s
34	
35	So: a bad `--key1` masks a bad `--data`. A bad `--key2` masks a bad `--data`.
36	
37	## 2. Encoding
38	
39	`str.encode()` is **UTF-8**. Byte length, not character length, is what AES sees.
40	
41	* `--key1 'ÀÁÂÃÄÅÆÇÈÉÊËÌÍÎÏ'` (16 chars, 32 bytes) → valid AES-256 key.
42	* `--data 'ÀÁÂÃÄÅÆÇ'` (8 chars, 16 bytes) → valid block.
43	
44	### Invalid UTF-8 in argv (surrogateescape)
45	
46	CPython decodes `argv` with `surrogateescape`, so byte `0xFF` becomes `U+DCFF`.
47	`.encode()` then raises, exit code **1**:
48	
49	* one offending run of surrogates, length 1:
50	  `UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode character '\udcff' in position 0: surrogates not allowed`
51	* a run of length > 1:
52	  `UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 5-7: surrogates not allowed`
53	
54	`position` is a **character** index into the str; only the **first** offending run is reported.
55	`\udcXX` is rendered lowercase-hex, 4 digits.
56	
57	Node's `process.argv` is lossy (invalid bytes → `U+FFFD`), so raw bytes must be recovered from
58	`/proc/self/cmdline` (NUL-separated, Linux) and decoded with a surrogateescape decoder.
59	Fall back to `process.argv` when `/proc/self/cmdline` is unreadable.
60	
61	## 3. AES
62	
63	Standard AES (FIPS-197), single block, ECB, **no padding**.
64	
65	* key must be exactly 16, 24 or 32 **bytes** → AES-128 / AES-192 / AES-256
66	  otherwise `ValueError: Invalid key size`
67	* plaintext block must be exactly 16 bytes → otherwise
68	  `ValueError: plaintext block must be 16 bytes`
69	
70	Verified reference values:
71	
72	| key1 | key2 | data | line 1 | line 2 |
73	|---|---|---|---|---|
74	| `0123456789012345` | `0123456789012345` | `0123456789012345` | `b'_}\xf0\xbf\x10:\x8cJ\xe6\xfa\xad\x99\x06\xac;*'` | `b'0123456789012345'` |
75	| `012345678901234567890123` | `0123456789012345` | `0123456789012345` | `b'-v\x01Eg>BY\xder\xee\\*uJg'` | `b'*9\xc6\x81\xc5y\x8f\r\xff$\xb2\xb5@\x01(\x97'` |
76	| `01234567890123456789012345678901` | `0123456789012345` | `0123456789012345` | `b']\x99\x81D\xe9O\x14F[}9\xf4<\xf1\x8aW'` | `b'#R\xd9\xc5\xa3\x0f\x9f 2%\xe7\x13~R\x10\xf2'` |
77	
78	132 more vectors in `/workspace/harness/vectors.json`.
79	
80	## 4. `repr(bytes)` — Python 3 exact rules
81	
82	Emit `b` + quote + body + quote.
83	
84	* Quote choice: `'` normally. If the bytes contain `0x27` (`'`) **and not** `0x22` (`"`), use `"`.
85	* Body, per byte:
86	  * `\\` for `0x5C`
87	  * `\t` `\n` `\r` for `0x09` `0x0A` `0x0D`
88	  * the quote char itself, escaped as `\'` or `\"` — only when it equals the chosen quote
89	  * printable ASCII `0x20`–`0x7E` verbatim (this includes space, `"` when quote is `'`, and `'` when quote is `"`)
90	  * everything else → `\xNN`, lowercase hex, 2 digits
91	
92	Measured:
93	
94	| data | line 2 |
95	|---|---|
96	| `abc'def"ghi\jklm` | `b'abc\'def"ghi\\jklm'` |
97	| `abcdef'ghijklmno` | `b"abcdef'ghijklmno"` |
98	| `abcdef"ghijklmno` | `b'abcdef"ghijklmno'` |
99	
100	Note `\x0b`, `\x0c`, `\x00`, `\x7f` all use `\xNN` (Python bytes repr has **no** `\v`, `\f`, `\a`, `\b`, `\0`).
101	
102	## 5. argparse emulation
103	
104	`prog` = `os.path.basename(sys.argv[0])`. In Node use `basename(process.argv[1])` → `test15.mjs`.
105	
106	### Help (`-h`, `--help`, or any unambiguous prefix like `--h`, `--he`) → stdout, exit 0
107	
108	```
109	usage: test15.mjs [-h] --key1 KEY1 --key2 KEY2 --data DATA
110	
111	options:
112	  -h, --help   show this help message and exit
113	  --key1 KEY1
114	  --key2 KEY2
115	  --data DATA
116	```
117	
118	Note: help wins even if required args are missing, and even if it appears **after** valid args.
119	Help text column: `help_position = min(action_max_length + 2, 24)` where
120	`action_max_length = max(len(invocation)) + 2`; invocations are `-h, --help` (10),
121	`--key1 KEY1` (11), … → `action_max_length = 13`, `help_position = 15`.
122	`"  -h, --help"` is 12 chars → 3 spaces of pad. Actions with no help string emit just the
123	invocation line.
124	
125	### Errors → stderr, exit 2, always preceded by the one-line usage
126	
127	```
128	usage: test15.mjs [-h] --key1 KEY1 --key2 KEY2 --data DATA
129	test15.mjs: error: <message>
130	```
131	
132	Measured messages:
133	
134	| argv | message |
135	|---|---|
136	| *(empty)* | `the following arguments are required: --key1, --key2, --data` |
137	| `--key1 K` | `the following arguments are required: --key2, --data` |
138	| `--DATA K --key2 K --data K` | `the following arguments are required: --key1` |
139	| `-key1 K --key2 K --data K` | `the following arguments are required: --key1` |
140	| `--key1 K --key2 K --data K --extra x` | `unrecognized arguments: --extra x` |
141	| `--key1 K --key2 K --data K positional` | `unrecognized arguments: positional` |
142	| `--key1 K --key2 K --data K --` | `unrecognized arguments: --` |
143	| `--key K --key2 K --data K` | `ambiguous option: --key could match --key1, --key2` |
144	| `--k 1 --key2 2 --data 3` | `ambiguous option: --k could match --key1, --key2` |
145	| `--key1` | `argument --key1: expected one argument` |
146	| `--key1 --key2 K --data K` | `argument --key1: expected one argument` |
147	| `--key1 -abcdefghijklmno …` | `argument --key1: expected one argument` |
148	
149	Required-argument errors are raised **before** the unrecognized-arguments check
150	(`--DATA K --key2 K --data K` reports only the missing `--key1`).
151	
152	### Value-vs-option classification (argparse `_parse_optional`)
153	
154	A token is treated as a **value** (not an option) when:
155	* it is empty, or does not start with `-`
156	* it matches `^-\d+$` or `^-\d*\.\d+$` **and** the parser has no negative-number-like option
157	  strings → `--key1 -123456789012345` is accepted as a value
158	* it contains a space → `--key1 '- 123456789012345'` is accepted as a value
159	
160	Otherwise a leading `-` makes it an option token → `--key1 -abcdefghijklmno` errors.
161	
162	### Other behaviors
163	
164	* `--key1=VALUE` form works, including with abbreviations (`--dat=VALUE`).
165	* Later occurrences overwrite earlier ones (`--key1 A --key1 B` → `B`).
166	* A leading `--` makes everything after it a positional; with no positionals defined, this
167	  yields the required-arguments error. A **trailing** `--` survives as
168	  `unrecognized arguments: --`.
169	* Option order is irrelevant.
170	
171	### stderr encoding
172	
173	`sys.stderr` uses `errors='backslashreplace'`, so a surrogate that reached an argparse message
174	is written as the literal 10-byte text `\udcff`:
175	
176	```
177	$ test15_executable --key1 K --key2 K --data K $'x\xffy'
178	test15_executable: error: unrecognized arguments: x\udcffy
179	```
180	
181	(Measured with `od -c`: `x \ u d c f f y`.) stdout never carries non-ASCII, because
182	`repr(bytes)` is pure ASCII.
183	
184	### Terminal width
185	
186	Usage and help wrap at `shutil.get_terminal_size().columns - 2`.
187	`get_terminal_size` honours `$COLUMNS` first, then the real terminal, else `(80, 24)`.
188	When output is piped (the normal grading case) width is `80 - 2 = 78` and nothing wraps.
189	
190	`COLUMNS=30` (width 28) — prog too long, so prog goes on its own line and the option
191	group is wrapped with a 7-space (`len('usage: ')`) indent:
192	
193	```
194	usage: test15_executable
195	       [-h] --key1 KEY1
196	       --key2 KEY2 --data
197	       DATA
198	```
199	
200	`COLUMNS=40` (width 38) — prog fits, hanging indent is `len('usage: ' + prog + ' ')`:
201	
202	```
203	usage: test15_executable [-h] --key1
204	                         KEY1 --key2
205	                         KEY2 --data
206	                         DATA
207	```
208	
209	and the help column wraps too:
210	
211	```
212	  -h, --help   show this help message
213	               and exit
214	```
215	
216	## 6. Unhandled-exception output (exit 1)
217	
218	stdout is **empty**; stderr gets a CPython traceback. Source-echo lines appear only when
219	`test15.py` happens to sit in the cwd, so the piped/graded form is:
220	
221	```
222	Traceback (most recent call last):
223	  File "test15.py", line 20, in <module>
224	  File "test15.py", line 12, in main
225	  File "pyaes/aes.py", line 304, in __init__
226	  File "pyaes/aes.py", line 134, in __init__
227	ValueError: Invalid key size
228	[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test15' due to unhandled exception!
229	```
230	
231	Frame stacks measured:
232	
233	* `Invalid key size` → `test15.py:20 <module>`, `test15.py:12|13 main`,
234	  `pyaes/aes.py:304 __init__`, `pyaes/aes.py:134 __init__`
235	* `plaintext block must be 16 bytes` → `test15.py:20 <module>`, `test15.py:14 main`,
236	  `pyaes/aes.py:342 encrypt`
237	* `UnicodeEncodeError` → `test15.py:20 <module>`, `test15.py:12|13|14 main` (no pyaes frames)
238	
239	## 7. Hard constraints on the port

All 73 checks pass (exit 0). Final deliverables, all ESM `.mjs` with `.mjs`-suffixed relative imports, zero dependencies, no `node:crypto` reference anywhere (including comments):

- `/output/lib/aes/galois.mjs` — `xtime`, `gmul`, `ginv` (inverse table built by exhaustive search at load; `ginv(0) === 0`)
- `/output/lib/aes/tables.mjs` — `SBOX` derived algorithmically (`ginv` + affine `b ^ rotl1..4 ^ 0x63`), `INV_SBOX` by permutation inversion, `RCON` via repeated `xtime`, and `MUL2/3/9/11/13/14`; throws at import if the FIPS-197 spot values, the `INV_SBOX[SBOX[i]] === i` identity, or the RCON sequence fail
- `/output/lib/aes/errors.mjs` — `InvalidKeySizeError` (defaults to `'Invalid key size'`), `InvalidBlockSizeError(message)`
- `/output/lib/aes/key-schedule.mjs` — `BLOCK_SIZE`, `ROUNDS_BY_KEY_SIZE`, `isValidKeySize`, `expandKey` returning `{ keySize, rounds, roundKeys }` with round keys pre-flattened into block byte order (AddRoundKey is a plain 16-way XOR)
- `/output/lib/aes/block-cipher.mjs` — `AES` class with `keySize`/`rounds` getters and non-mutating `encryptBlock`/`decryptBlock` (straightforward inverse cipher; `TypeError` on non-16-byte blocks), re-exports `BLOCK_SIZE`
- `/output/lib/aes/index.mjs` — re-exports `AES`, `BLOCK_SIZE`, `expandKey`, `isValidKeySize`, `ROUNDS_BY_KEY_SIZE`, both error classes
